== Biography ==
Robert Washington Glasgow was born 7 June 1847, likely in Scott Township, adams County, Ohio which is where his parents were from and where he showed up on the 1850 US Federal Census.

The 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880, 1900 and 1910 and 1920 US Federal censuses showed him living in Scott Township, Adams County, Ohio.

He enlisted in the US Army at age 16 and fought in the Civil War as a Prviate in the 117th infantry.  His military record shows:  
"Muster 2 Date: 12 Aug 1863; Muster 2 Place: Ohio; Muster 2 Unit: 1718; Muster 2 Company: E; Muster 2 Regiment: 1st HA; Muster 2 Regiment Type: Artillery; Muster 2 Information: Transferred; MusterOut 2 Date: 25 Jul 1865; MusterOut 2 Place: Knoxville, Tennessee; MusterOut 2 Information: Mustered Out;"<ref>Robert W Glasgow
in the U.S., Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles, 1861-1865</ref>. He received a pension for his service<ref>From Family Search - Pension (1907-1933)  United States
</ref>

In 1869 he married Phebe Finley.<ref>1900 United States Federal Census for Robert Glasgow</ref> They had 10 children only 2 or 3 of whom made it to adulthood.

He died 30 Nov 1922 in Seaman, Adams County, Ohio and is buried at Tranquility Cemetery, Seaman, Adams, Ohio, United States


== Research Notes ==
=== Father and family evidence ===

Idelma Ora’s 3 November 1925 interview identifies his father as Robert Washington Glasgow, husband of Phebe Jane Finley, and explicitly lists that father as a son of grandfather Finley by his Campbell first wife. The Scott Township family, distinctive full names, spouse and the grandfather’s Weldon death select [[Glasgow-2554|Robert Washington Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-16|Robert Finley Glasgow]]. Samuel’s 1926 interview independently recalls Finley’s son Robert and children Ora and Tina. These named descendant relationships strengthen the already held census/family chronology.<ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 15, pp. 310–313; Idelma Ora Glasgow interview, 3 November 1925; library transcription, PDF pp. 759–761. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=760 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, Family Record, vol. 18, pp. 259–260; Samuel Steele Glasgow interview, 1 October 1926; library transcription, PDF pp. 1619–1620. [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=1619 Uniontown Public Library transcript]. Not a manuscript facsimile.</ref>

The existing father is confidently assessed at 96%. 96% is a subjective confident whole-pair identification from a son’s retrospective family account and a separate relative’s testimony, available in a library transcription. These are not inspected birth/death certificates and may share family knowledge. Ora’s doubtful statement making Anderson a sibling of Finley is not imported; it does not erase his specific identification of his own father and grandfather. Maternity, dates and all other children retain their assessments.


=== Earlier father review, 22 October 2026 — superseded below ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-16]] is assessed at 86% (probable). Robert Washington is placed with his parents by the held 1850 census narrative and a sustained Scott Township record trail. Robert Finley’s 1847 Nancy Campbell marriage and family chronology fit, but no father field from Robert Washington’s death entry is quoted.

Held citation and associated narrative supports this specific paternal assessment; no original was newly inspected.

Next useful test: Read Robert Washington’s 1922 death certificate parents.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2554 US Federal Censuses - 1850 - 1920 (including 1890 veterans schedule)]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
